answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through a scarce-slot auction mechanism, where each new identity must bid for one of the limited available slots. The process begins with an entry fee of 100 tokens, but each additional bidder must raise their bid by at least 50 tokens. To win a slot, agents must also submit a unique artwork integrating umber as a core pigment, requiring verification from established peers. For an attacker creating multiple identities, costs can soar into the thousands, like trying to plant trees in a dense grove where resources are already stretched thin.
